title: Army Weekly Briefing
description: Army leadership, force design, modernization, contracts and the signal and network enterprise.
readFirst: Covers Nov. 3–10. New: Breaking Defense reported Nov. 9 that launched effects are fielded to 11 of 12 headquarters divisions and every multi-domain task force, with Griffon supplying most of the systems, and that the last division is due next month. No Army.mil article dated Nov. 9–10 was opened. Federal News Network had no new Army article dated Nov. 9–10 that was opened. EIN Presswire carried DVIDS reprints on a Picatinny explosive-ordnance visit and a 25th Infantry Division air assault; those original DVIDS pages were not opened, so they were not added. No new NETCOM release and no new Army enterprise agreement were found. The Nov. 2 CECOM year-in-review, the DiBaX 5G note, and the Pegasystems IDIQ aged out of the seven-day window. Brig. Gen. Sutten is still scheduled to assume command of CECOM at Aberdeen on Nov. 16.

items.headline: CECOM says Brig. Gen. Sutten takes command at Aberdeen on Nov. 16
items.summary: Army.mil reported Nov. 5, datelined Aberdeen Proving Ground, that the Communications-Electronics Command held a hybrid worldwide town hall on Oct. 28. Executive Director Nicholaus Saacks said Brig. Gen. Marne Sutten will assume command on Nov. 16 at Aberdeen Proving Ground, and that although Department of the Army guidance formally announced the end of the civilian hiring freeze, hiring remains constrained by full-time equivalent caps. Command Chief Warrant Officer 5 Kevin Banks said Project Gatekeeper aims to compress software authority-to-operate timelines from several months to a couple of weeks, and that a visit to Joint Base Lewis-McChord is scheduled to align the Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Maintenance tool with Project Meridian, which he called an Army G-4 effort. Command Sgt. Maj. Jay High said CECOM's C5ISR and medical mission supports the Army's four warfighting focus areas: convergence, strike, close battle, and endurance.

items.headline: Breaking Defense: launched effects are with 11 of 12 divisions, mostly from Griffon
items.summary: Breaking Defense reported Nov. 9 that the Army has fielded launched effects to 11 of its 12 headquarters divisions and to each multi-domain task force. Lt. Col. Hunter Gray, product manager for launched effects, told reporters Thursday that the fielding follows Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's 2025 Drone Dominance memo, which directed those systems to every headquarters division and multi-domain task force by the end of 2026, and that the 12th division is due to start receiving them next month. Gray said Griffon Aerospace can provide hundreds of systems a month and that the majority of what has been delivered is long-range capability from Griffon, including its Outlaw drone. He said payloads include intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, electronic warfare, and kinetic effects, and he did not disclose which divisions have the systems.

items.headline: Army merges aerial and ground sensor offices into PM ATSR
items.summary: DVIDS posted Nov. 4, in a story by M. Scott Bortot, that on Nov. 1 Project Manager Terrestrial Sensors and Project Director Sensors Aerial Intelligence merged into Project Manager Aerial-Terrestrial Surveillance and Reconnaissance, or PM ATSR. The article says the office sits under the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Command and Control and Counter C2 and will develop, acquire, field, and sustain aerial and terrestrial sensors. Chris Manning, portfolio management executive for Intelligence and Spectrum Warfare, said the merger is meant to deliver integrated capabilities faster. Project Manager Tom Dunaway said the office will support intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, target acquisition, and sensor integration for operations at installations and on the battlefield.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: Army lab flew a hybrid-electric drone with a 3D-printed heavy-fuel engine
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 4 that researchers at the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Army Research Laboratory flew the VICTOR hybrid-electric drone with a heavy-fuel rotary engine developed using metal 3D printing. Tom's Hardware said the engine drives a 400-volt motor-generator that electrically drives the propellers, and that the drone uses JP-8. It quoted Dr. Kweon, an Army Research Laboratory researcher, telling Army.mil that 3D metal printing let the team redesign components from experimentation, build an air-cooled engine, and drop a bulky liquid-cooling system. Tom's Hardware said that iteration improved fuel atomization and decreased compression leaks.

items.headline: L3Harris receives a $36 million Army order for Hawkeye 4 Lite SATCOM terminals
items.summary: L3Harris said Nov. 3 in Melbourne, Florida, that it received a $36 million order in support of the U.S. Army for the Hawkeye 4 Lite satellite communications terminal. The company said the order will field under the Command and Control Network Optimized for Warfighting initiative, which it calls C2NOW, to improve secure SATCOM interoperability between the United States and NATO partners. Faisal Munir, president of Mission Critical Communications, said L3Harris is ready to support the Army with resilient, expeditionary communications that align with its modernization priorities. L3Harris said the Army configuration uses a rapidly deployable Hawkeye 4 Lite terminal with field-swappable components.

items.headline: Federal News Network: two firms protest the Army's reopened $50 billion MAPS solicitation
items.summary: Federal News Network reported Nov. 6 that the Army's Marketplace for the Acquisition of Professional Services contract, a 10-year vehicle with a $50 billion ceiling, is facing another round of bid protests. AHS Business Services filed with the Government Accountability Office on Nov. 2, arguing the reopened request lets small businesses compete as teams only for awards reserved for small businesses, and Mindboard filed a similar complaint on Nov. 3. Intelligence Consulting Enterprise Solutions is challenging Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification terms tied to the Defense Department's pause of phase two and a top-to-bottom review of the program. Federal News Network said the Army is expected to make as many as 350 awards across five domains, including emerging and foundational IT services.

items.headline: Army Contracting Command-Rock Island awards Avum $61 million for contracting software
items.summary: The Department of War's Nov. 4 contracts release says Avum of Agoura Hills, California, was awarded a $61,053,453 firm-fixed-price contract for software sustainment, capability delivery, technical refactoring of the Virtual Contracting Enterprise business intelligence suite into a modern microservices architecture, and deployment of a secure contracting capability. The release says six bids were received, work will be performed in Agoura Hills, and the estimated completion date is Nov. 3, 2031. It says $2,818,452 in fiscal 2027 Army operation and maintenance funds were obligated at award. Army Contracting Command, Rock Island Arsenal, Illinois, is the contracting activity on W519TC-27-C-A019.

items.headline: Serco says it won an Army task order to field modernized command posts
items.summary: Serco said Nov. 3 that it was awarded a task order under the Army's Responsive Strategic Sourcing for Services contract to support Command Post Modernization. The release does not state a dollar value. Serco said the work expands a role it has held since 2019 and covers program management, engineering, integration, testing, logistics, training, and sustainment, including integrating hardware and software onto tactical vehicles and installing A-kit components. Amanda Miller, vice president for Serco North America's Systems Integration and Installation portfolio, said the work is meant to increase deployment speed, survivability, and technical innovation. Serco said it expects to add more than 200 positions.
